Keeping your toes healthy is important for overall foot care. Wash your feet daily with mild soap and dry them well, especially between the toes, to prevent moisture buildup. Trim your nails straight across to avoid ingrown toenails. Wear comfortable, breathable shoes that fit properly to prevent pressure and irritation. Moisturize your feet but avoid applying lotion between the toes to reduce the risk of fungal infections. The footing of a wall or a slab is the lower part of the foundation that supports the weight of the structure and prevents settling. Footings are wider and thicker than the other parts of the walls or slabs they support, and they stabilize the structure, support it and ideally they prevent settling.  Footings or footers are especially important in instable soils.  #footing #retainingwall #slabongrade #blockwall #structuralengineering #landscapewalls

videos.caption: Why is this footing so deep? 👀 If you’re walking your jobsite and see a section dug deeper than the rest, that can actually be a good sign. It may mean the operator found a stump, soft soil, or unsuitable material and took the time to dig it out instead of building over it. We also perform soil compaction testing to help identify areas that aren’t suitable to build on. If we find bad soil, we excavate it until we reach suitable, solid material that passes testing and gives that footing a strong foundation. Don’t be scared of a deep footing—be concerned about the builder who ignores what’s underneath it. “Therefore whosoever heareth these sayings of mine, and doeth them, I will liken him unto a wise man, which built his house upon a rock:” — Matthew 7:24 #diy #newhome #footing #foundation #homebuilder
